Worcestershire Accident and Emergency staff thanked with coffee and cake as hospitals prepare for busy winter

Claire Bullivant 3 hours ago   0 Comments

HARDWORKING A&E staff at two Worcestershire hospitals have been treated to coffee and cake as part of a nationwide initiative recognising the efforts of emergency department teams.

Around 200 workers at Worcestershire Royal Hospital and the Alexandra Hospital in Redditch were thanked for their dedication during special events organised by the charity Rapid Relief Team (RRT).
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:37
Instaread

The visits formed part of the charity’s second annual A&E Appreciation Week, which saw more than 400 volunteers organise over 130 events at 100 hospitals across the UK.

More than 10,000 emergency department workers were recognised nationally through the initiative, which aims to boost staff morale and acknowledge the pressures faced by frontline NHS teams.

The events come as new research commissioned by RRT suggests widespread public concern about the pressures facing emergency services.

Staff enjoying a well-earned coffee and cake break at Worcestershire Royal Hospital during AandE Appreciation Week

A survey of 2,063 UK adults found that 79 per cent of respondents in the West Midlands believed A&E staff did not receive sufficient recognition for their work.

It also found that 61 per cent of respondents in the region said they would think twice about attending A&E this winter because of the pressures facing the NHS.

Meanwhile, 80 per cent of those surveyed in the West Midlands supported allowing A&E staff to refuse treatment to patients who were abusive.


Peter Francis, RRT Local Team Leader, said:

“As winter approaches, A&E teams are preparing for an incredibly busy period, but they rarely get the thank you they deserve. Sometimes, they even get abused for just doing their job.

“A&E Appreciation Week aims to shine a spotlight on the incredible efforts A&E staff put in. It was great to see staff at Worcestershire Royal and Alexandra Hospital enjoying coffee and cake to give them a little boost and to know that their work is truly valued.

“We hope this gesture will help them understand the public has their back when things get tough on shift.”

At Worcestershire Royal Hospital, the event also brought together hospital staff and colleagues from West Midlands Ambulance Service.

Samantha Watson, Senior Sister and Ward Manager in the hospital’s Emergency Department, welcomed the initiative.

She said:

“We were delighted to host our second event with the Rapid Relief Team and received such a warm welcome from the volunteers.

“It was wonderful to learn more about the fantastic work RRT carries out behind the scenes and to share the event with our WMAS colleagues, who we work alongside so closely. Everyone appreciated the event, and it was a reminder of how much those small acts of kindness can brighten a busy day.”

The charity is now calling for A&E Appreciation Week to become an officially recognised annual national event.

Its research found that two-thirds of respondents supported the proposal, while 77 per cent believed NHS workers had received greater public appreciation during the Covid pandemic than they do today.

Ross Norman, RRT UK Head of Operations, said the events were a small but meaningful way of acknowledging the contribution made by emergency department workers.

“A coffee and a slice of cake won’t fix the pressures on the NHS, but it’s a chance for staff to stop for a few minutes and hear that people are grateful. We want to see A&E Appreciation Week officially recognised so that it happens every year.”

The Rapid Relief Team is a volunteer charity associated with the Plymouth Brethren Christian Church, providing practical assistance to emergency services, charities and communities.

Alongside A&E Appreciation Week, the organisation launched its Nurses Community Connect initiative in August, providing 4,000 hot meals to nurses, patients and their families across the country.
